**🔎  | MATCH UP BASICS  **

- Falco's bread and butter, **uptilt**, is **-12 on shield **if he starts it from the *front*.** WAIT FOR THE SECOND HIT, THEN PUNISH WITH FARORE'S WIND!!! **

- **Farore's Wind's *first hit*** is the **easiest and most reliable way to punish ALL of Falco's moves** (besides down tilt & up air.)

- **Falco's down tilt is +11 frames on shield, meaning we cannot do anything to punish it - PERIOD!**

**🚨  | STAGE BANS **

- Yoshi’s *[platform extensions, easy for him to recover up the sides, Zelda can't ledge trap with Phantom, instant ban everytime]*
- Town & City *[platform extensions, can take advantage of the higher ceiling better than Zelda can]*
- Kalos *[easy for him to recover up the sides, can use the platforms to escape Zelda's ledgetrapping]*
- Battlefield (**can be interchanged based on comfort level**) *[platform extensions, can take advantage of the higher ceiling better than Zelda can]*

author: katyparry
content:
**DETAILED REASONING:**

- Falco's bread and butter, **uptilt**, is **-12 on shield**. We must buffer our punish/jump as soon as the second hit touches our shield. **WAIT FOR THE SECOND HIT, THEN PUNISH WITH FARORE'S WIND!!! **You can even stay in shield and let him do a second up tilt if you need more time. (as long as your shield is fresh, or aimed UP)

- **Farore's Wind's *first hit*** is the **easiest and most reliable way to punish ALL of Falco's moves** (besides down tilt & up air.)

 We get this for free *every single time*, and can teleport away to reposition. **I believe its better to use this as a movement tool, rather than attempting to kill Falco will the second hit.** Falco can out do us in the air, and **if he DI's the move** (which is likely because he wants to move after landing his uptilt to cover OUR DI) and we tried to chase him, **he can easily upair/bair/any aerial really and kill us off the top.**

- **Falco's down tilt is +11 frames on shield, meaning we cannot do anything to punish it - PERIOD!** Most Falcos will down tilt again after connecting the first one at lower percents, because they are waiting for their opponent to swing in disadvantage. Once you show them you aren't going to Nayru's/attack back in disadvantage, they will start to chase you with their jump. Nairdodge will beat this, but they can call it out with a short hop fast fall aerial.

author: _stubz
content: If you notice Falco responding to fully charged phantom at ledge with jump out of ledge hang and immediate reflector, running up with dtilt covers this/cancels the reflector and allows a pop up into phantom. Even though reflector is frame one on Falco, dtilt still beats it out when executed out of Falco's ledge jump (tested by and confirmed with Ray). Because Falco jumps back slightly in the process of reflecting, you don't even have to space the dtilt. You can throw it out right at the edge of the stage. If reflector hits you, in most cases it will break the knight or you will be in the windbox zone, so you take a small amount of damage as the primary immediate risk in this scenario until the Falco changes up their play and chooses to jump fair you for it, etc.

author: ticomaster
content: <a:6mcgoddessservingnayru:1343320090984054817> **Reflector Counterplay** at mid-range, the closer the Reflector is to you, the safer you are. If he's reflecting and the blue reflector is coming *towards you*, the phantom won't hit you. It only hits you if the blue reflector is coming *back to him* and it's reflected at that moment.
